paper_title: Learning to Reason under Off-Policy Guidance
caption: : Ratio of clipped signals.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the ratio of clipped signals over training steps for two methods, with an x-axis labeled “Steps” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500 and showing major tick labels at 0, 200, and 400, and a y-axis labeled “Clip Ratio (%)” on a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20. The “On-policy” series is drawn as a solid dark-blue line with no markers; it rises quickly from near 0 at the start to roughly 0.06 within the earliest steps, then fluctuates mostly between about 0.04 and 0.06 through the mid-range (e.g., around steps 200–400 it stays near ~0.05 with small oscillations), and ends near roughly 0.055–0.06 by step 500. The “Mixed-policy w/ Shaping” series is drawn as a solid red line with no markers; it begins near 0 at step 0, jumps sharply to a peak slightly above 0.20 (around ~0.21) very early, then drops to around the 0.12–0.15 range and continues with noticeable fluctuations across steps (including intermittent local rises around ~0.15), trending to values around ~0.10–0.12 in the later portion and finishing near roughly 0.10 by step 500.
